title: 1999 AHSME Problem 27
statement: In triangle \(ABC,\) \(3\sin A + 4\cos B = 6\) and \(4\sin B + 3\cos A = 1.\) Then \(\angle C\) in degrees is

solutions.text:
Squaring both equations and adding gives \[ \begin{aligned} &9 + 16 \\ &\quad {}+ 24\small(\sin A \cos B + \cos A \sin B) \\ &\quad = 37, \end{aligned} \] so \(24\sin(A + B) = 12\) and \(\sin(A + B) = \tfrac12.\)

Then \(\sin C = \sin(A + B) = \tfrac12,\) so \(\angle C = 30^\circ\) or \(150^\circ.\) If \(\angle C = 150^\circ,\) then \(A \lt 30^\circ,\) making \(3\sin A + 4\cos B \lt 6,\) a contradiction. Hence \(\angle C = 30^\circ.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
